title: Moving Models
summary: Models have no single Position — move them with PivotTo (the modern way), or translate the PrimaryPart's CFrame with SetPrimaryPartCFrame for older workflows. Welded assemblies move together; loose parts scatter.

explanation.whatItIs: The 'models aren't parts' playbook: pick the sanctioned API for relocating a whole assembly at once.
explanation.whyItExists: A model is a container, not a physical object — the engine offers pivot-based movement as the sanctioned route.
whenToUse: model:PivotTo(cframe) — moves the entire model (anchored + unanchored), preserving internal layout
SetPrimaryPartCffset-style offsetting when you must keep the PrimaryPart semantics (older codebases)
whenNotToUse: Moving individual parts of a welded model manually — you'll tear it apart
Physics-driven motion — use forces on a BasePart instead
explanation.mentalModel:
```text
Model = container of parts
  └─ the "where" is the PIVOT (GetPivot())

Move everything:
  model:PivotTo(newCFrame)

Read 'where is it?':
  model:GetPivot().Position
```
tips: PivotTo works on Humanoid characters too (teleports respect collisions reasonably)
For smooth motion, tween a placeholder or Lerp the pivot in Heartbeat — but mind physics
Weld all parts so physics moves them as one unit
commonMistakes: Setting .Position on parts inside a welded model individually — assembly fights itself
No PrimaryPart/Pivot expectation and 'jumps' when moving
PivotTo-ing unanchored assemblies mid-air without considering momentum

examples.title: Teleporting an NPC
examples.code:
local npc = workspace.NPCs.Guard

-- Where is it?
local cf = npc:GetPivot()
print("NPC at", cf.Position)

-- Teleport 20 studs north, keeping orientation:
npc:PivotTo(cf * CFrame.new(0, 0, -20))

-- Face the player while teleporting:
local target = workspace.CurrentPlayers.Raani.Character.HumanoidRootPart.Position
npc:PivotTo(CFrame.lookAt(cf.Position, target))
